title: Antihypertensive use was linked to slightly longer time without recorded cognitive impairment
summary: In a retrospective All of Us analysis targeting a high-risk population with model-derived weights, baseline antihypertensive use was associated with slightly longer time without a first recorded mild cognitive impairment diagnosis. The ratio of geometric mean time capped at 48 months was 1.012 overall and 1.026 in a subgroup with cardiometabolic and depressive multimorbidity.

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 §4 propensity/outcome models, logistic risk weights, sample construction, Table 3 and Figure 3

evidence.tested: The study trained its risk model in a non-overlapping internal reference set of 83,745 participants and estimated associations in a 37,577-participant analysis set with 500 first recorded MCI diagnoses within 48 months. Model-derived weights target a high-risk population without restricting the cohort to a directly observed high-risk stratum.
evidence.unknown: The estimates are associations involving baseline medication use and the first recorded diagnosis. Treatment initiation, adherence, causal benefit and external validation were outside the study.
evidence.ai_role: A regularized logistic model fitted to the non-overlapping reference sample estimates target high-risk membership; cross-fitted XGBoost models estimate treatment propensity and outcomes.
